title: Does the SEKA Exceed Weigh-Up to Tier-1 Mainstream? (for 1/2 the price)

takeaways.text: He gives about AU$11,500 (US$8,000) for the complete project build; by publication the frameset and wheels had each dropped about US$300, and frames were sold by deposit with a 12-week lead time.

His medium build with SRAM AXS 1×, a Rival power meter and 60 mm wheels weighed 7.5 kg with pedals; he lists the frame at 885 g, the uncut fork at 383 g, the 100 × 400 mm integrated bar at 350 g and the wheels at 1,460 g.

A carbon specialist's ultrasound found the frame consistent and well made but very thin, with little margin for error; the creator could not vouch for durability for riders over about 90 kg on harsh roads.
He describes the geometry as relaxed for an aero bike and the ride as softer and less aggressive than the stiffest aero frames he has ridden.
Like other direct-from-China frames, he expects less warranty and support infrastructure than mainstream brands, which lowered his practicality score.
At 179 cm he normally rides size 54 with a 100 mm stem; he found this frame slightly short in reach and would have fitted a 110 mm stem.

disclosure: The creator calls this a sponsored project: retailer Cycling 100 gave him the frameset and wheels and paid him for selected videos, including this one; he says he earns no sales commission. The frame is the Exceed RDC; the candidate dealer build does not state whether it uses the RDC or standard Exceed frame.
summary: A July 2022 long-term review of a medium SEKA Exceed RDC built with SRAM AXS 1× and 60 mm wheels, with weights and a carbon specialist's ultrasound view. The dealer build listed here may use the RDC or the standard frame.
